chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Maysab is that which Salman (peace be upon him) was contracted for, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, bestowed it upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), thus it is in her charities.

key_terms.أَفَاءَهُ: He bestowed it / He made it flow (referring to divine bestowal of property)
key_terms.صَدَقَتِهَا: Her charities (referring to the charitable endowments of the Prophet's family)

ai.seo_question: What is Al-Maysab and how did it become part of the Prophet's family charities?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the legal status of 'Al-Maysab' (often identified as the garden of Banu Nadir or a specific property of Salman) as a *sadaqah* (charitable endowment) of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, establishing its exemption from Zakat and inheritance. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Prophet’s personal properties, once designated for charity, remain under the stewardship of the Imams, reflecting the continuity of spiritual and material authority within the household of revelation.
